national.title: Dolores Huerta, labor activist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
national.summary: Dolores Huerta was a labor activist and civil rights leader who co-founded the group that later became the United Farm Workers.
national.body: Dolores Huerta, the labor activist and civil rights leader who co-founded with Cesar Chavez the group that later became the United Farm Workers, has died, her family said in a statement posted to social media. She was 96.Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home."As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the family said. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning."Huerta kept a busy schedule well into her 90s, marching in protests and speaking in cities across the country about race, poverty, LGBTQ+ and women's rights on behalf of her Bakersfield, California-based foundation.Huerta's resolve cemented her place in history as one of the nation's most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists. Her three-word Spanish-language slogan "Sí se puede" — which translates to "Yes, it can be done" — was grounded in the belief that people could affect change.Her work over the decades earned her a number of accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor. When then-President Barack Obama presented the award in 2012, he praised Huerta as a tenacious leader and joked that he had stolen her slogan for his 2008 campaign.This year, Huerta sent shockwaves through the Latino community when she revealed that she was sexually abused in the 1960s by Chavez, leading to the birth of two children, a secret she kept for 60 years and long after he died.From the early 1970s on, Huerta's life partner was Richard Chavez, César's brother, and together they had four kids. She also had seven children from two earlier marriages.Huerta said she had kept silent for so long because she feared that coming forward would compromise her life's work and unravel all the progress made for workers.When asked during a 2026 interview with the news organization Latino USA about keeping the secret, Huerta said: "It was my personal pain, it was my personal problem and, you know, I think it was worth it because it was my cross to bear. I'll say it that way."

national.title: US civil rights leader Dolores Huerta dies aged 96
national.summary: Huerta fought for farm workers' rights in the 1960s and 1970s and had continued to work addressing immigration and voting issues.
national.body:
US civil rights leader Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96, her family has announced.

Huerta campaigned alongside fellow labour leader Cesar Chavez for farm workers' rights in the 1960s and 1970s, founding the United Farm Workers Union (UFW) with him.

Through her foundation, Huerta had continued her activism work addressing immigration and voting issues.

"As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," family spokesman Erik Olvera said on Wednesday.

Earlier this year, Huerta said Chavez, who died in 1993, had "manipulated and pressured" her into having sex and on another occasion forced her in the 1960s.

That was after the New York Times published an investigation detailing allegations from Huerta and two other women, who said Chavez groomed and sexually abused girls involved in the labour movement.

Huerta said the two encounters with Chavez resulted in pregnancies that she chose to keep these secret, arranging for the children to be raised by other families.

Chavez's family said in a statement at the time that they were "devastated" by the reports and praised the women's "courage to come forward".

national.body: Israel's defense minister on Wednesday denounced opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot for urging the military to resist post-election pressure from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has threatened new strikes on Iran. "His call to senior military officials not to obey the directives of the prime minister or me or of other relevant security authorities, on the grounds that 'they have his support,' is an anti-democratic statement detached from reality," Israel Katz wrote on X . Eisenkot, a former military chief, said in a speech to supporters after Tuesday's election that Netanyahu was a caretaker prime minister lacking a mandate and the military should serve the state rather than the premier. "Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you. You have my unequivocal backing. Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Eisenkot said. Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened in recent days to renew strikes on Iran. Media reports, denied by Netanyahu, said military chief Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir pushed back immediately before the election on the prime minister's new plans on Iran. Eisenkot's comments were the latest in "a campaign of lies" about tension between Netanyahu and the military over Iran, Katz said.

national.title: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
national.summary: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry.
national.body:
Dolores Huerta is seen at the California Democratic Party's 2025 State Convention at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, May 31, 2025. Court Mast/AP hide caption

Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry, has died. She was 96.

Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home.

She kept a busy schedule well into her 90s, marching in protests and speaking in cities across the country about race, poverty, LGBTQ+ and women's rights on behalf of her Bakersfield, California-based foundation.

Huerta's resolve cemented her place in history as one of the nation's most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists. Her three-word Spanish-language slogan — which translates to "Yes, it can be done" — was grounded in the belief that people could affect change.

Dolores Huerta is seen at the California Democratic Party's 2025 State Convention at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, May 31, 2025. Damian Dovarganes/AP hide caption

Her work over the decades earned her a number of accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor. When then-President Barack Obama presented the award in 2012, he praised Huerta as a tenacious leader and joked that he had stolen her slogan for his 2008 campaign.

This year, Huerta sent shockwaves through the Latino community when she revealed that she was sexually abused in the 1960s by the farmworker movement's co-founder, César Chavez, leading to the birth of two children, a secret she kept for 60 years and long after he died.

national.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
national.summary: Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him.
national.body:
Areej Hazboun, Associated Press Areej Hazboun, Associated Press

Audrey Horowitz, Associated Press Audrey Horowitz, Associated Press

JERUSALEM (AP) — Anxious Israelis watched election results near completion Wednesday after the highest voter turnout in over a quarter-century, as no clear winner emerged and weeks of negotiating could lie ahead for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and an array of opposition parties trying to unseat him.

Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it's not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel.

Netanyahu seeks to remain the country's longest-serving prime minister. In defiant comments after the vote — which showed his Likud party losing ground since the 2022 election — he dismissed as treasonous the idea of partnering with Arab parties.

On Wednesday, Netanyahu warned against a "dangerous government" that might include them. He won't work with the Arab-led parties, whose constituents make up 20% of Israel's population, and they have also ruled out any partnership with him.

His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group.

But it's not clear whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office.

national.title: Dozens dead in Spain after high-speed train slams into another stopped on tracks
national.summary: At least 68 people were killed in the country's second deadly rail collision this year.
national.body:
Joseph Wilson, Associated Press Joseph Wilson, Associated Press

Iain Sullivan, Associated Press Iain Sullivan, Associated Press

URDA, Spain (AP) — One high-speed Spanish train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and shredding carriages in the country's second deadly rail collision this year.

The regional government for Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people needed medical treatment in hospital. Rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies.

The accident comes with memories still fresh of another crash between high-speed trains in southern Spain in January involving trains from the same two companies.

Spain's rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, involving two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital Madrid to Seville in southwestern Spain.

One train, run by the state-owned RENFE company, ran into the tail of the other train owned by private company IRYO that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track in a rural area between two villages.

David Gómez, a construction worker, was working with his brother and another colleague nearby when they heard the crash and ran to help, he told the newspaper El País.

national.title: Cornell faculty to begin voting on no-confidence measure over handling of sexual assault allegations
national.summary: Cornell University faculty will meet Wednesday to conclude debate and begin voting on a proposed no-confidence resolution in the university's administration following widespread frustration over its response to a woman who reported she was gang raped at a campus fraternity house in 2024.
national.body:
Leah Willingham, Associated Press Leah Willingham, Associated Press

Cornell University faculty will meet Wednesday to conclude debate and begin voting on a proposed no-confidence resolution in the university's administration following widespread frustration over its response to a woman who reported she was gang raped at a campus fraternity house in 2024.

The meeting comes after an Oct. 14 Faculty Senate meeting at which angry members confronted Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff about the university's handling of the allegations.

The meeting was closed to the media, but in an audio recording obtained by The Associated Press, Kotlikoff acknowledged some missteps, defended his leadership and asked for more time to push for cultural changes in student social life and make reforms. He urged faculty to have confidence in his leadership, pointing to an independent investigation into the university's handling of the case that he said could lead to meaningful reforms.

A woman identified in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe filed a lawsuit last month alleging that seven Chi Phi fraternity members sexually assaulted or exploited her in October 2024 and that Cornell mishandled her complaints. All seven men have denied her allegations.

WATCH: Fraternity culture under scrutiny in wake of Cornell allegations

The criminal investigation by Cornell's police department stalled after the district attorney declined to pursue charges. In a New York Times interview, Kotlikoff said he never followed up to learn what had happened to the woman or the investigation.

Asked by a faculty member whether he read the Cornell Police Department's report on the rape allegations, Kotlikoff acknowledged he had not, but said that was because the police investigation was confidential and university policy is that top administrators shouldn't have a role in criminal investigations.

national.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
national.summary: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the incident occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.
national.body:
Two trains have collided in Spain just south of the capital Madrid on Wednesday morning.

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

So far at least 68 people are confirmed to have died in the incident.

The two trains collided just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) between municipalities Mora and Orgaz, and about 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid.

The accident happened when a high-speed train travelling from Madrid to the south of the country collided with another train that was apparently stationary. The crash caused at least two carriages to fall down an embankment.

Broadcaster RTVE, quoting the transport ministry, said a Renfe train rear-ended an Iryo train.

Renfe is Spain's national state-owned railway company while Iryo is a private high-speed railway operator.

All train traffic on this line has been stopped at stations along the route, Adif said.

national.summary: Fed officials will unveil their latest interest rate move this week, following the September rate hike, the first in three years.
national.body: The Federal Reserve will announce on Wednesday whether monetary policymakers are raising interest rates for the second time this year in a bid to subdue inflation. Most economists and Wall Street analysts expect the Fed to leave its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4%. Consumer prices have surged this year, with headline inflation across the U.S. rising at a 3.7% annual rate in September as energy costs jumped. Core inflation, which excludes volatile energy and gas categories, rose 2.6% from a year ago amid signs inflation could be seeping into the broader economy. The Fed targets annual inflation of 2%.Gasoline prices, which have hovered above $4 a gallon for the last three months, accounted for more than half the September increase in consumer prices, according to the Labor Department."Although the latest hot inflation readings and rise in inflation expectations will concern Fed officials, they still appear broadly intent on tightening policy at a measured pace," Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist at investor advisory firm Capital Economics, said in a recent research note.In September, the Fed raised the federal funds rate — what banks charge each other for overnight loans — by a quarter of a percentage point — its first hike in three years, thereby raising borrowing costs across the U.S. economy. The Fed is scheduled to announce its latest interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday.The meeting comes at a crucial time, as Americans head to the polls to cast their ballots in the midterm elections on Nov. 3. national.title: Nearly 75% of ex-NFL players who died from 2008-2023 had CTE, study finds
national.summary: Nearly 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had CTE, a new study out of Boston University finds.
national.body: Nearly 75% of NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a new study led by Boston University researchers finds.CTE is a degenerative brain disease that is found in people who have suffered repeated blows to the head. It can only be definitively diagnosed after death. CTE has been discovered in football players as well as other athletes, first responders and military members.The study published in JAMA Network Open shows how CTE, rarely seen in the general population, is far more common among deceased NFL players, lead author Julia Gallini said in a statement."With CTE consistently found in less than 1% of donors to community brain banks, an estimated 75% prevalence among NFL players who died over a 16-year period is concerning, and suggests we need to increase efforts to support families, diagnose CTE during life, and treat CTE-related symptoms," Gallini said.CTE study findingsB.U. said the new findings build on a study released in August, which estimated that anywhere from 25% and 98% of ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE. "The wide range reflected uncertainty about how representative brain donors were of the overall NFL population," B.U. said in a statement. "Brain donors are more likely to have symptoms believed to be related to CTE, a concept known as selection bias." In the new study, 362 of 387 deceased ex-players were found to have some form of CTE. But to counter the selection bias, researchers factored in that former NFL players with cognitive symptoms were five times more likely to have their brains donated to science."They used this estimated selection ratio to adjust the 94% prevalence of CTE observed among brain donors to an overall estimate of 74.5%," B.U. said. The authors noted that the study only involved NFL players who have died and does not predict how many living former or active players might have CTE. "It's hard to learn what the guys who built the game have suffered through," former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck, an ambassador for the study, said in a statement. "We have to learn from this data to make the game safer, because we can't accept these numbers for the next generation of players." national.body:
Daniel Kozin, Associated Press Daniel Kozin, Associated Press

Mauricio Savarese, Associated Press Mauricio Savarese, Associated Press

MIAMI (AP) — Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Wednesday after fleeing Brazil.

Watch Bolsonaro's arrival in the U.S. in the video player above.

The stunning move came after 48 hours in which Bolsonaro refused to concede to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and then threatened to attempt to annul the election result .

Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula before returning to Brazil three months later. On Monday, the U.S. said that it would grant visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family. Bolsonaro, a Trump ally, visited the White House in May.

Bolsonaro first fled from Brazil to Argentina and then Ecuador alongside his wife and two daughters, Argentina's migration authority said Wednesday — a day after the 45-year-old senator and his family were granted United States visas by the Trump administration.

Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases. The court had ordered Bolsonaro to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday — two days after he lost the vote to Lula. It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said late Tuesday he also has an Italian passport.

national.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
national.summary: With 85% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.
national.body:
With 85% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither the incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, nor the bloc of his key challenger Gadi Eisenkot look set to have a majority.

In order to form a government, it looks likely one of the leading parties would have to break their campaign promises - meaning the most probable outcome may well be new elections.

Could Netanyahu persuade Eisenkot to join him in a national unity government?

Eisenkot would have to abandon his key platform to do so. He's framed himself as the only alternative to Netanyahu, and built his campaign on ousting him from power.

Just last night, he took to the stage at his campaign HQ and called on Netanyahu to "announce his retirement from political life today," telling the crowd that Israelis are fed up with Netanyahu's "culture of lies", "division and incitement".

But that was before one of the main exit polls - which had initially projected a lead for Eisenkot's bloc - was revised, and he was overtaken by Netanyahu.

Netanyahu could try to persuade Eisenkot's Yashar Party to join his Likud Party in a unity government by ditching the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties he is currently in coalition with. But last night at Likud HQ he thanked his "loyal partners" and called for a "strong right-wing government"- remarks some have interpreted as meaning he intends to preserve his alliance with them.

One thing that could make a unity government more likely is a renewed conflict with Iran, which could place serious pressure on party leaders to put aside their political differences and work together. In the days prior to the election, Israeli and US media reported that Netanyahu was pushing for fresh strikes on the country, and had pressed Donald Trump to approve US involvement.

national.title: WATCH LIVE: Fed chair Warsh holds briefing after latest interest rate decision
national.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to stand pat on interest rates Wednesday even though inflation has accelerated in the past couple of months as the Iran war has caused spikes in oil and gas prices.
national.body:
Christopher Rugaber, Associated Press Christopher Rugaber, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Federal Reserve is expected to stand pat on interest rates Wednesday even though inflation has accelerated in the past couple of months as the Iran war has caused spikes in oil and gas prices.

Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh is expected to hold a news conference at 2:30 p.m. EDT. Watch live in our video player above.

The Fed's latest policy meeting concludes less than a week before the midterm elections, which have focused heavily on concerns about the cost of living and affordability. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items.

The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation. The Fed raised its key rate last month for the first time in three years, from about 3.6% to 3.9%, in what many investors and economists perceived was a first step toward a renewed effort to bring down inflation.

Yet Warsh faces a host of challenges in achieving that goal. President Donald Trump slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank's rate-setting committee, rather than Warsh, whom he appointed. And some of the forces driving inflation — specifically the rapid buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure and higher energy prices — won't easily be tamed by higher interest rates.

At the same time, other parts of the economy are already being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month, though it has since slipped a bit. Higher mortgage rates have made buying a home unaffordable for 5 million more Americans since the beginning of the year, according to Oxford Economics, a consulting firm. Over time, Fed rate hikes can make mortgages, auto loans, and credit card borrowing more expensive, adding to Americans' sense that things like homes and cars are getting pricier.

After the Fed announces its rate decision, Warsh will speak at a news conference, where his remarks will be closely watched for hints about the Fed's next steps. He will likely repeat the Fed's desire for a "timelier" return of inflation to the 2% target. Some may view that as a sign the Fed will boost its key rate at its next meeting, in December, a move already widely expected by Wall Street investors.

national.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
national.summary: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.
national.body:
As prices have ticked up in recent years, the cost to caregivers has skyrocketed. A study, released Wednesday by AARP and shared first with NPR, finds that family caregivers — people helping out disabled, chronically ill or elderly adults — now spend an average $11,508 out of pocket each year. That's roughly 60% more than just five years ago, and adds up to 31% of a caregiver's income, on average.

Only on NPR Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know The increase during those years is more than twice the overall rate of inflation of 24%, as measured by the federal Bureau of Labor Statistics' Consumer Price Index.

What's driving the ramp-up? Food, housing and medical expenses are the biggest chunk, finds the study, which queried 2,538 family caregivers.

The bump in costs comes as family caregivers take on more care and more complicated medical responsibilities at home, says Megan O'Reilly, vice president of governmental affairs at AARP. "The more care that's needed, the more it costs."

What It Takes Why is caregiving so hard in America? The answers emerge in a new film And increased spending is only part of the story. The demands of caregiving often require people to reduce their working hours or quit work entirely, the survey finds. It's a double whammy: increased costs on top of lost income.

Meghan Maher has seen that first-hand. Just seven weeks after the birth of her first baby, her mother was diagnosed with advanced cancer. Suddenly, Maher was a "sandwich" caregiver — parent and child needing her at the same time.

Meghan Maher and her mom Connie Cadwell. In order to help her mother through cancer treatment and care for her young children, Maher had to leave her career. Maher family hide caption

At first, she tried to manage it all. She returned to her career in cancer research after maternity leave, but keeping up with the demands of work, her mom and her newborn son was too much.

national.body: The U.S. military said it attacked a boat it accused of smuggling drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean on Tuesday, killing five people, as the Trump administration continues its campaign against alleged traffickers in Latin America. The latest attack brings the number of people who have been killed by the U.S. military's boat strikes to at least 240 in more than 70 strikes. national.title: U.S. cruise ship suspends around-the-world voyage due to fuel costs
national.summary: The U.S. cruise ship MV Odyssey suspended its three-year, around-the-world voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.
national.body: Sihanoukville, Cambodia — A U.S. cruise ship on an around-the-world voyage that touted its cabins as floating homes suspended its three-year voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to disembark.The MV Odyssey set sail two years ago on a voyage to the seven continents marketed as combining long-term living at sea with global travel. Its operator had offered to "make the Odyssey your permanent home," with the purchase price of a suite for the lifetime of the vessel starting at around $230,000. For now, it is docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with no certain departure date.The ship has been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, according to Cambodian officials. It has a 650-passenger capacity. Its Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, said monthly fuel expenses per cabin that historically averaged $1,800 have reached an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia due to the war in Iran. The company said it sought to reduce fuel consumption by slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port, but was unable to offset the surging costs. Traffic has been curtailed in the Strait of Hormuz since the war in Iran began, squeezing supplies of all kinds of petroleum-based fuels, especially in Southeast Asia, and sharply increasing prices.The average price for a gallon of diesel fuel the day before the war started, Feb. 27, 2026, was $3.76, according to AAA, and was $6.52 late last month, an increase of $2.76. "We have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses," Villa Vie Residences said in a statement issued Tuesday. "Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution. Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees" while it tries to restructure. "The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements," it said. However, a blogger who has been on the cruise, Randy Cassingham, wrote online that "the company has done absolutely nothing to help: we couldn't even walk out of the port, so there were shuttle buses that dropped us in the middle of town, Sihanoukville, Cambodia." "They didn't even give us a list of hotels, let alone help us get there or pay for them," Cassingham said on his website. The company could not immediately be contacted for comment.

Democrats in the US Congress are already planning how they would use their power if they win a majority in the House or Senate in next week's midterm elections.

Success is by no means guaranteed, even if midterms can sometimes be brutal for the incumbent party that holds the White House.

Control of the chamber, however, would give the party power to issue subpoenas - summons to testify or produce documents - as well as additional funding to launch investigations early next year.

Democrats are weighing whether to investigate senior figures in the Trump administration - and possibly the president himself. Staffers have begun assembling a list of possible investigations and witnesses, according to people familiar with the discussions.

Here are a few potential Democratic targets if the party emerges victorious on 3 November.

Democrats have made it clear that lucrative deals brokered by the Trump family's vast business empire will be primary targets of any initial investigations.

"We want to make sure that [American] taxpayer dollars are being used wisely and not being stolen or pocketed because of corruption," Virginia Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam, a member of the House Oversight Committee, told the BBC.

Items under consideration for investigation include ties between the administration and corporate entities - particularly cryptocurrency firms - as well as the international business dealings of the president's son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

national.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot face difficult paths to power as neither set to win majority
national.summary: The two main blocs appear to have too few seats to form the next government without reliance on Arab parties.
national.body:
With results still trickling in, it currently appears that Israel's veteran Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has done better than was widely predicted, with his Likud emerging as the largest single party.

His existing bloc with ultra-nationalist and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties appear to be just short of a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat parliament. However, analysts caution that this is subject to change because the early count was skewed towards areas known to have strong right-wing support.

A dramatic deadlock had been widely forecast as Israelis surged to the polls – with turnout reaching more than 77%.

In Israel's fragmented political system, the signs are that Netanyahu's main rival, the former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, would struggle to command a parliamentary majority without parties led by Israel's Arab minority. According to partial results, they have equalled or gained on their previous record number of seats.

On the campaign trail, most Jewish opposition parties pledged not to work with Arab-majority lists, citing a lack of shared values.

However, Israel's Arab-led parties could emerge as kingmakers if others were prepared to join forces with them. In this election, Arab Israelis – who often identify as Palestinian citizens of Israel and represent one-fifth of the population – appeared to turn out in unprecedented numbers.

Netanyahu, on the other hand, would need to convince one of the smaller opposition parties to join his coalition, if he is to secure a majority at this point.

Israeli exit polls suggest no clear winner with Eisenkot's bloc neck and neck with Netanyahu

national.title: Luxury cruise passengers stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs
national.summary: The Villa Vie Odyssey suspended its voyage and is working with passengers on "temporary living arrangements".
national.body:
A luxury cruise ship on a years-long voyage around the world said it suspended operations due to extraordinarily high fuel costs, leaving passengers stranded in Cambodia.

The US-based operator of the Villa Vie Odyssey said it was working with passengers on disembarkation plans and "temporary living arrangements".

It is unclear how many were on board but the nearly 200m (656ft) vessel can carry up to 650 passengers. It departed Belfast in October 2024 for a "continuous voyage around the world".

Global fuel prices have soared since the Iran war started earlier this year. The ship's operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 (£6,000) from $1,800.

Villa Vie Residences said it had taken "significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port". But those measures turned out to be insufficient to "offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs".

"Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," it said.

The company would spend the next 60 days on "restructuring and recapitalisation", though "no outcome is assured", it said.

There were reportedly around 200 passengers on board when they were ordered to disembark in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, a once sleepy beach town that has gained global notoriety in recent years as a hub for Chinese casinos and scam centres.

national.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
national.summary: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.
national.body:
Tanzania has announced a significant discovery of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay area in the south of the country - the first such find in a decade.

Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the Kasa-1X ST2 well, which is jointly owned by state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and French oil firm Maurel & Prom, to mark the occasion.

He said the estimated 223 billion cubic feet (6.3 billion cubic metres) discovery was a "major milestone" in the development of the small oil and gas sector in the East African nation.

The new well is expected to start production early next month and is intended to boost domestic supplies.

Tanzania has existing natural gas reserves of 57.54 trillion cubic feet.

"The discovery is important in ensuring the country has reliable, clean and safe energy at affordable costs, particularly at a time when demand is increasing due to industrial growth and other economic activities," Homera said.

Natural gas accounted for nearly 80% of Tanzania's sources of electricity generation, according to government statistics for 2024.

In recent years, the country has also encouraged the use of compressed natural gas to power vehicles, with natural gas plants and filling stations set up mostly in the largest city, Dar es Salaam.

national.title: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
national.summary: Authorities say the attacker in Belgrade was an underage male who was being monitored by security services.
national.body:
Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in the early hours of Wednesday after what authorities called a "terrorist attack".

The country's interior minister, Ivica Dacic, said the attacker had rushed at a police officer with two knives while shouting the phrase "Allahu Akbar". The officer sustained a minor knife wound to the face and shot the attacker.

Dacic said the suspect has not been identified, but he was a minor and Serbian citizen who was being monitored by security services as he was "known to be a supporter of the Islamic State".

Speaking to reporters outside the embassy, Dacic said an investigation is ongoing, but security services said the suspect had posted a picture of the Islamic State flag on his Instagram.

Dacic raised the country's terrorism threat level to "red alert" - the highest threat level – meaning stricter security checks and increased police presence at places like infrastructure facilities and areas where large crowds gather.

The interior minister said he had visited the injured police officer, who was reportedly doing well and did not need hospital care for his wounds.

Armed security personnel were seen standing guard outside the Israeli embassy on Wednesday morning.

Israel's foreign ministry confirmed in a social media post that no embassy personnel were injured and the mission was closed at the time of the incident.

national.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
national.summary: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.
national.body:
Emergency services attend to the victims at the scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Wednesday. Juanma Jiménez/Europa Press via AP hide caption

URDA, Spain — One high-speed Spanish train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and shredding carriages in the country's second deadly rail collision this year.

The regional government for Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people needed medical treatment in hospital. Rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies.

The accident comes with memories still fresh of another crash between high-speed trains in southern Spain in January involving trains from the same two companies.

Spain's rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo, involving two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital Madrid to Seville in southwestern Spain.

One train, run by the state-owned RENFE company, ran into the tail of the other train owned by private company IRYO that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track in a rural area between two villages.

This framegrab taken from a video provided by Spain's Guardia Civil shows an aerial view of carriages and first responders on the site of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, Wednesday. Guardia Civil via AP hide caption

David Gómez, a construction worker, was working with his brother and another colleague nearby when they heard the crash and ran to help, he told the newspaper El País.

local.body:
The Fredonia Board of Trustees has officially called for the removal of Flock Safety license plate-reading cameras from the community.

The board voted 4-1 Monday on the resolution requesting that the Chautauqua County District Attorney's Office remove the devices.

"While I acknowledge the system could be very valuable to law enforcement, there are some inherent problems with it," said Trustee Ben Brauchler.

"There was no resolution passed (by trustees) for this agreement to be in place," Trustee LeeAnn Lazarony said. "Therefore, I think the contract should be null and void, as it wasn't through resolution by the Board of Trustees to authorize the mayor to sign the Flock Camera agreement."

Trustee Tim Mulholland said he echoed Lazarony's sentiments in voting "aye," and Trustee Christine Cruz Keene offered her affirmative vote without comment.

In an unusual move, Trustee Paul Wandel requested to vote last. It seemed like Wandel recognized that he was the only opposition to the resolution, and wanted the last word on it.

Wandel read excerpts from a Sept. 14 email to village officials by District Attorney Jason Schmidt. The DA defended his Flock program at a trustees' meeting around the time of his email.

"I believe each and every one of us want the same things," Schmidt wrote. "To live in a safe community free of government overreach, to know our tax dollars are being spent smartly and cost effectively, and to ensure that our children and younger population have a full and fair opportunity to better themselves and rise above their beginning circumstances."

local.title: Local couple brings semipro basketball back to Rochester
local.summary: Chaniah Martino and Howard Jeffries are the owners of The Rochester Reapers Organizations, a men's semiprofessional basketball team.
local.body:
Rochester is once again home to a semiprofessional men's basketball team. The Rochester Reapers became part of the American Basketball Association league earlier this year.

The owners, Chaniah Martino and Howard Jeffries, are a young couple who found a way to fuse both of their passions to create this new organization.

"Once I realized that basketball was something he loved and business was something I loved, I figured we might as well put it together," said Martino.

The former caterer brought the idea to her fiancé, with three team name options. They both agreed that "Reapers" was most suitable.

"They're on demon time," Martino said to describe her players, using a slang term for a state of rigor and tenacity. "They're not coming to play."

The team's roster consists of veteran and rookie ABA players who have established comradery on and off the court. Jeffries said he intentionally drafted a group of men who he believes are "out for the same mission."

"The guys that I've picked are guys that I know want to work together," Jeffries said. "They're going to do anything it takes to get the win."

The Reapers are not Rochester's first professional or semi-pro team. The Rochester Seagrams formed in 1923 but in 1945, when they joined a forerunner to the NBA, they became the Rochester Royals. The team moved to Cincinnati in 1957 and exists today as the NBA's Sacramento Kings.

local.title: Attorney general needs to stick to law
local.summary: Saritha Komatireddy isn’t a household name for many New Yorkers. And that’s too bad, because she could be your next state Attorney General. We know all too well what we will get statewide by electing Letitia James as attorney general – more lawsuits that are so tinged by party politics that it’s har
local.body:
Saritha Komatireddy isn't a household name for many New Yorkers. And that's too bad, because she could be your next state Attorney General.

We know all too well what we will get statewide by electing Letitia James as attorney general – more lawsuits that are so tinged by party politics that it's hard to discern whether or not the case makes sense. That happens, in part, because James has been smacked down by courts often enough in her attempts to fill her prior campaign pledges to make life hard on President Donald Trump that it's hard to tell where a case actually exists or if James is just pandering to her supporters.

In our view, that shouldn't be a question when it comes to the state's attorney. Let’s not forget the First Department Appellate Division throwing out a $464 million liability verdict against Trump and the Trump Organization in August 2025 that was ruled to violate the Eighth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Earlier this year James led a multi-state coalition of 19 attorneys general suing the Trump administration over executive orders giving Elon Musk’s DOGE access to federal payment systems that was dismissed by a federal judge.

James is also fond of saying the Attorney General’s office doesn’t have a hand in local criminal cases while backing Democratic Party-backed policies like bail reform, Raise the Age, decriminalization of minor offenses, cashless bail, discovery reform and others.

Komatireddy, on the other hand, has said during her campaign that she will try to chart a bipartisan path forward to fix New York’s bail system, including pushing reform that allows judges to consider someone’s dangerousness when considering bail. She would also use her office to help local prosecutors by sending attorneys to help with manpower and prosecutions.

The most striking difference between James and Komatireddy, however, is a willingness not to abandon fairness for political points. We have seen time and again that James is an attorney general who doesn't hide her opinions, whether those opinions are in regard to President Donald Trump or the Cornell University fraternity rape allegations. We need an attorney general who keeps their opinions to themselves and lets the law be their guide. As a federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of New York, Komatireddy has prosecuted high-profile cases involving international terrorism, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, fraud, and foreign public corruption while arguing before federal courts, leading national security investigations and advising on matters of foreign affairs, criminal law, and cyber policy.

local.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. (AP) -- If the Baltimore Ravens play like they did in the second half against Cincinnati, not even Lamar Jackson can save them.

Already facing a reputation for folding late in games, the Ravens were a caricature of themselves Sunday, outscored 35-0 in the final two quarters of a 35-13 loss to the Bengals. Jackson missed a third straight game with an ankle injury, Baltimore didn’t take full advantage of its statistical domination in the first half and then Cincinnati scored touchdowns on its first five possessions of the second.

The Ravens have outscored opponents by 65 points in the first half this season, while being outscored by 70 in the second. First-year coach Jesse Minter suggested the issue is at least partly psychological -- Baltimore isn’t handling momentum swings very well. He also indicated Monday that the team could use more leadership from players.

“There’s moments in the game where it’s like, ‘Who’s the guy that’s going to grab everybody together and get them together on the sideline?’ As a team we’re working through who that is,” Minter said. “There’s guys that want to do it, and there’s guys that, maybe they’re dealing with something, or they’re not playing the way they want to play, so they don’t feel like they can do it in those moments.

“If you’re kind of a known leader, sometimes you have to even erase how you’re playing if you feel like you can collectively get everybody out of a funk,” he added. “Those are things I think we’re just continuing to work towards, but yeah, I think there’s moments where we need a little bit more.”

The Ravens are 4-3, which isn’t itself cause for panic, but that record also has Baltimore in last place in the AFC North. Now the Ravens have to play at Buffalo this weekend, then have a quick turnaround before a Thursday night home game against Jacksonville.

“I think he’ll be in a decent spot, but we’ll know a lot more on Wednesday,” Minter said.

The first half. More specifically, the Ravens -- even with Tyler Huntley at quarterback -- have started well in games offensively, with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle using receiver Zay Flowers impressively.

FALCONER -- A near full moon hung above the soccer pitch at Falconer High School Wednesday night as Jamestown Community College (JCC) earned a spot in the Region 3 women’s soccer championship game with a 2-1 victory over Herkimer College.

The opening minutes mirrored the final score, as both teams found space and tested the opposing goalkeeper in a back-and-forth battle.

In the 18th minute, sophomore Kaylyn Carnes put her boot to the ball, but Herkimer’s goalkeeper was up to the task, keeping the game knotted at 0-0.

The Generals had opportunities to net the game’s first goal in the 27th and 42nd minutes, but sophomore Angel Busch came up big, making two of her four saves on the night.

JCC had another chance to take the lead in the 37th minute, but Avery Johnson sent her shot just wide of the net, and the teams went into halftime scoreless.

That scoreless deadlock continued into the 83rd minute, when the intensity reached another level and the Jayhawks responded in front of a packed house filled with green and gold.

First, Kennady Ellsworth settled a ball in the box and tapped it over to Alexandria Halstrom, who buried the attempt to give JCC a 1-0 advantage.

The capacity crowd had barely finished celebrating when freshman Gracie Chimera finished an assist from sophomore Kaylyn Carnes. In less than a minute, Jamestown had built a 2-0 lead, sending Jayhawk Nation into a frenzy in the stands.

local.summary: The village of Fredonia water system appears in deep trouble again. It was hit with a boil order Tuesday, days after a conservation order. Fredonia had to buy 966,000 gallons of water from the city of Dunkirk over the weekend, Mayor Michael Ferguson said Monday at a regularly scheduled Board of Trus
local.body:
The village of Fredonia water system appears in deep trouble again. It was hit with a boil order Tuesday, days after a conservation order.

Fredonia had to buy 966,000 gallons of water from the city of Dunkirk over the weekend, Mayor Michael Ferguson said Monday at a regularly scheduled Board of Trustees meeting.

The boil order was announced by the village Office of Emergency Management at 8:45 a.m. Tuesday morning. The stated reason for the order was "High turbidity levels and treatment deficiencies."

Fredonia water customers should bring water to a rolling boil for at least one minute, then let it cool before using for: drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, making ice, food preparation and washing produce, and preparing baby formula.

Officials will conduct "Water sampling after levels stabilize. The order will remain in place until testing confirms the water is safe," the Office of Emergency Management order stated.

The boil order is likely tied in with the conservation order, which officials say was spurred by recent dry weather which taxes the filters at the reservoir.

Ferguson said at the Monday evening village Board of Trustees meeting that Dunkirk transferred 966,000 gallons of water to Fredonia over the weekend, through a pump station on Vineyard Drive.

Ferguson said the flow from Dunkirk was shut off Monday morning. He acknowledged, "The draw for water is more than we can produce right now. Hopefully that changes shortly."

local.body:
A bagpiper in a kilt led hundreds of Azusa Pacific University students and the school president into the Cougars’ stadium before kickoff against Whittier College earlier this season, a sun-splashed celebration of what once were two of the biggest brands in California small-college football.

Azusa Pacific had dropped the sport in 2020 after 55 years and Whittier in 2022 after 115 years, mainly for financial reasons.

The two are back on the field, not in a full reembrace of the sport’s tradition and what it can do to enhance campus culture, but for another reason: Administrators saw an opportunity to bump shrinking enrollment numbers, a problem shadowing hundreds of colleges and universities across the country. Football rosters, after all, can number about 100 players and the sport is seen as a popular marketing anchor.

The two schools are among 10 four-year colleges and universities that started or restarted programs this season, the most in a single year since 2013, according to the National Football Foundation. Seven schools have announced plans to start programs in 2027 or later.

Azusa Pacific won the 1998 NAIA Division I championship and became a full NCAA Division II member in 2013. The Cougars made playoff appearances in 2016 and ’18, but a decline in the number of West Coast Division II football schools made travel too costly.

School president Adam Morris said he first approached athletic director Gary Pine about restarting football five years ago. A $1 million private gift funded startup costs, and the school moved from Division II to Division III and joined a Southern California-based conference. APU will begin competition in women’s flag football in the spring.

“Yes, it’s an opportunity to grow enrollment and there is some financial upside to the decision,” Morris said. “Really, it’s a great opportunity to touch the lives of 110 young men who will leave this place to go out into this community and have an impact in a significant way.”

APU’s on-campus fall enrollment is 1,900, down 46% from 3,359 in fall 2020. APU brought in 652 freshmen (49 were on the football roster) and transfer students to campus this fall, up 19% from a year ago. The school’s online learning program raises total enrollment to about 6,000.

local.summary: October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to recognize the importance of early detection, regular screening and improving women’s health. local.body:
October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to recognize the importance of early detection, regular screening and improving women's health. It is also an opportunity to talk about prevention and the steps we can take to reduce the risk of cancer.

Smoking remains the leading cause of preventable disease and death. In New York State, 9.9% of adults smoke cigarettes and 6.3% use e-cigarettes. And for women, smoking has been marketed to us as glamorous, stylish, fierce, and trendy... even a way to control weight. However, tobacco use contributes to cancer and negatively impacts every organ in our body. Women who smoke for more than 10 years appear to have approximately 10% higher risk of developing breast cancer compared to/with women who have never smoked.

Breast Cancer Awareness Month reminds us that screening can save lives, and prevention and healthy lifestyle choices matter too. Helping women -- and all New Yorkers -- break free from smoking and nicotine-use should be part of routine health care. Furthermore, smoking-related health care costs New York an estimated $12.07 billion each year.

Through Health Systems for a Tobacco-Free WNY, we work with health care and behavioral health organizations to strengthen tobacco screening, treatment and cessation support. Our goal is to ensure that every patient who uses tobacco is offered evidence-based support to quit. Learn more at: Health Systems for a Tobacco-Free NY (HSTFNY)

For New Yorkers who are ready to make a quit attempt, the NYS Quitline provides free and confidential support. This October, the Quitline is also promoting its Quit to Win Pet Campaign, giving New Yorkers another reason to take that important first step toward quitting. Find more information at: Quit for Your Pet! – NY Smoke Free.

Let's remember that protecting women's health goes beyond screening. We can ensure people have the tools and knowledge they need to live long, happy, healthy lives.

Amanda Hucksoll is an employee at Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center.

local.summary: A former Buffalo school on South Park Ave. is set to become a new winter weather shelter. Erie County is leasing the property, but a city lawmaker is opposed to the plan.
local.body: A former Buffalo school building is set to become a winter weather shelter for people experiencing homelessness. Erie County has already approved the deal, but a Buffalo lawmaker is raising concerns.Starting November 1, Erie County is entering into a multi-year lease-agreement with Ellicott Development to turn the former Buffalo Creek Academy at 514 to 528 South Park Avenue into a 200-bed shelter. Erie County Executive Mark Poloncarz told me it's part of the state's Code Blue program and will act as a secondary location alongside Buffalo City Mission."We need it, it's as simple as that," Poloncarz said. "I wish we didn't. I wish we had people who were not homeless or needing temporary assistance but when people are homeless you gotta help them."WATCH: Former Buffalo school to become winter Code Blue shelterThe county is required by state law to provide shelter to those experiencing homelessness during inclement weather, when the temperature drops below 32 degrees fahrenheit. But Buffalo Common Councilmember Leah Halton-Pope is speaking out against the plans. local.title: City garbage truck strikes and kills man in a wheelchair
local.summary: Capt. Greg Bello said officers responded to Hudson Avenue and Warsaw Street around 3:30 p.m. for the report of a pedestrian struck and found the man dead at the scene.
local.body:
A man in a wheelchair was struck and killed by a Rochester garbage truck Tuesday afternoon, city police said.

Capt. Greg Bello said officers responded to Hudson Avenue and Warsaw Street around 3:30 p.m. for the report of a pedestrian struck and found the man dead at the scene.

Police said the garbage truck was traveling east on Warsaw Street and trying to make a left turn onto Hudson Avenue. The man was operating his motorized wheelchair northbound in the shoulder of Hudson Avenue when the truck hit him, police said.

In a statement, Mayor Malik Evans shared his "deepest condolences to the family and friends" of the man who died.

"Members of my City team are committed to conducting a thorough investigation to determine how this accident happened and what can be done to prevent further tragedies like this one," Evans said. "We will share updates as the investigation progresses."

The truck driver, a man in his 50s, was not injured. Police said it doesn't appear that drugs or alcohol were a factor.

The incident remains under investigation and anyone with information, including video, is encouraged to call 911.

local.body: After state and federal radiological testing found dangerous conditions near Gill Creek in the Town of Niagara, neighbors are asking for permanent relocation, not just temporary housing.It has been a long year for Lexi Hawk. She’s received letters from the State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), seen employees at her house sample soil and received test results that led the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to temporarily relocate her family.Just three blocks away from Lexi’s house, one of her neighbors, John Johnson, also got his test results back, and the radioactivity levels were so high that his family too was relocated.However, a few dozen people are living in the areas in and around their two homes that were never moved out during the testing or as remediation draws near."I want to get them to safety too," Hawk said. "I will always question what is beneath my feet. local.summary: The Buffalo man who admitted setting the fire that destroyed the Old Pink in Allentown was sentenced to five years in federal prison.
local.body: The Buffalo man who admitted setting the fire that destroyed the Old Pink in Allentown was sentenced to five years in federal prison.John Burns, 42, was sentenced Tuesday by U.S. District Court Judge Richard Arcara after pleading guilty in July to arson of a building used in interstate commerce.The fire destroyed the Old Pink at 223 Allen St. on June 17, 2024.Burns had been kicked out of the bar after getting into a fight and later returned with a blowtorch, setting a fire at the back of the building. The longtime Buffalo institution burned to the ground.Burns was arrested less than three months later and initially allowed to go to a rehabilitation facility.But in May of last year, he was remanded after allegedly removing an ankle monitor he was required to wear while awaiting trial.Burns had faced up to 20 years in prison.During Tuesday's sentencing, Burns appeared in an orange jumpsuit with his hands shackled in front of him. His parents and several other family members were in the courtroom to support him.Arcara said he had received 23 letters of support for Burns that discussed his struggles with mental health, substance abuse and alcohol.WATCH: 'Truly sorry': Buffalo man sentenced to 5 years for Old Pink arsonThe judge also received a handwritten letter from Burns just hours before the sentencing hearing.In the letter, Burns apologized for the fire."I would like to express my deepest apologies to the community of Buffalo for setting the fire that destroyed the Pink," Burns wrote, adding that he was "truly sorry."Arcara noted that the fire could have been catastrophic, but no one was injured.The judge sentenced Burns to 60 months in prison followed by three years of supervised release. Burns was also ordered to pay $708,519 in restitution.

entertainment.summary: Based on the Jane Austen classic, the streamer's take on the well-adapted story is written and executive produced by Dolly Alderton.
entertainment.body:
Elizabeth Bennett and Mr. Darcy are back in the official trailer for Netflix’s upcoming Pride and Prejudice adaptation. Based on the classic novel by Jane Austen, the limited-series stars Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden in the leading roles.

In the trailer, released Wednesday, the classic romance tale takes new life. “One day Jane, I shall be either a governance and a spinster or a wife and a mother,” Corrin’s Elizabeth, or Lizzie, tells her sister Jane Bennett, played by Freya Mavor. “And then finally we may talk about something else.” Related Stories Beyond the Book Free IP and Fresh Eyes: How Hollywood Is Reinventing the Classics Movies Frank Capra Was Darker Than You Think, Says Author of New Biography

Olivia Colman joins the young women as their mother, Mrs. Bennett. Rufus Sewell plays Mr. Bennett; Hopey Parish plays Mary; Hollie Avery plays Kitty; Rhea Norwood plays Lydia. The six-part series is written and executive produced by Dolly Alderton, with Heartstopper ‘s Euros Lyn serving as director.

“I got an email asking if I’d be interested in adapting Pride and Prejudice and my immediate response was, ‘I absolutely cannot do this. This is everyone’s favorite book. It’s too much responsibility,'” Alderton told Netflix’s Tudum . “I thought of all the things that could go wrong, and then I put that all in a box. Since then, I’ve just thought about the honor and the privilege of being entrusted with this story.”

Alderton’s take on Pride and Prejudice has been described as being faithful to Austen’s original novel. “ Pride and Prejudice is such a timeless story because of the emotions in the book; they are as pertinent now as they were in 1812,” Alderton added. Austen‘s Sense and Sensibility novel was also reimagined for feature film and released earlier this month.

Laura Lankester, Will Johnston and Louise Mutter for are executive producing for Lookout Point, alongside Alderton, Lyn and Corrin. Lisa Osborne is producing.

entertainment.title: Selena Gomez & Demi Lovato Reunite for Nostalgic Beauty Campaign: ‘Still Making Each Other Blush’
entertainment.summary: Two blush shades. One friendship.
entertainment.body:
The princesses are back. Nearly two decades after costarring in Princess Protection Program , Selena Gomez and Demi Lovato have reclaimed their tiaras for a special collaboration celebrating nearly 25 years of friendship.

As announced Wednesday (Oct. 28), Gomez enlisted Lovato for Rare Beauty’s new campaign, “Still Making Each Other Blush.” It arrives with a packaged set that includes two liquid blushes in different shades.

For the team-up, the two former Disney Channel stars posed in fancy gowns and crowns for some regal photos, marking one of the first times fans have seen them together in years. After meeting on Barney & Friends in 2002, Gomez and Lovato stayed close while building their careers as actresses and singers, starring on Wizards of Waverly Place and Sonny With a Chance , respectively, as well as costarring in Princess Protection Program (2009). There were a few bumps in the road that played out publicly over the years, but as of earlier this year, the artists are firmly in each other’s corners.

“I am in tears,” Gomez wrote on Instagram in April after attending one of Lovato’s It’s Not That Deep Tour concerts. “@ddlovato — this was hands down one of the best shows. Oh and the VOCALS? Psh *blown away.”

The Rare Beauty collab also builds on the wave of 2000s throwbacks that Disney stars such as Gomez and Lovato, as well as the Jonas Brothers and Miley Cyrus, have been enjoying this past year. The Jo Bros recently starred in a third Camp Rock film, adding to the franchise that launched Lovato’s career, while Cyrus produced a Hannah Montana 20th-anniversary special that featured a cameo from Gomez.

“I think the age that we’re at is really loving nostalgia right now,” Lovato told Billboard in April, noting that looking back on the golden era of Disney Channel has brought everyone closer recently. “For all the people who are in their 30s and have lived through the Disney era with me, Selena, the Jonas Brothers and Miley, they’re craving it, and it’s fun to go back and relive those moments.”

Lovato and Gomez’s blush duo is now available on Rare’s website .

entertainment.title: NFL Boss Roger Goodell Says ‘It Was Clear’ Jay-Z Wanted Super Bowl Halftime Show: ‘He’s Already Got His Vision’
entertainment.summary: Hov's heading to the West Coast.
entertainment.body:
Jay-Z was announced as the official Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show headlining performer earlier this week, but NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has long believed that Hov’s day on the Super Bowl stage would come.

Goodell joined Apple Music’s The Ebro Show for an interview with Ebro Darden and Eddie Francis on Tuesday (Oct. 27), during which he shed some light on the timing being right for Jay-Z to be the halftime show choice for February 2027 in Los Angeles.

“We’ve always wanted this to happen at some point. It was something I asked him about at the time when we first started this, and he said, ‘Yeah, we’ll see. Let’s see what happens.’ But it was clear he wanted it to happen,” Goodell explained. “We’ve talked about it a couple of times.”

The commissioner continued: “I think the fact that he’s in his 30th anniversary year of his first album, he just finished his tour, it’s L.A., he’s at that point as the GOAT that he’s ready for it. He was pretty clear: ‘I wanna do it this year.’ I guess I was more excited than anything, maybe a little surprised, because he keeps putting it off a little bit.”

Hov and Roc Nation have served as the league’s live music entertainment strategist since 2019. They re-upped in 2024 to extend their partnership, which has brought the likes of Rihanna , The Weeknd, Kendrick Lamar, Usher , Bad Bunny, Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg to the Super Bowl stage.

“But I think he’s already got his vision; he already understands what he wants to do,” Goodell added of Jay’s plan. “He’s been so remarkable in helping us elevate the whole Super Bowl Halftime Show. He’s a genius, and not just a creative genius in a musical sense. His business sense, his sense of timing, his sense of what’s necessary in the world — he’s just got that. I trust him, and I trust his point of view.”

As part of the NFL’s halftime show announcement, Goodell revealed that his one request to Jay when the NFL entered a partnership with Roc Nation was that the Brooklyn rap dignitary take the Super Bowl stage at some point.

“When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” Goodell said in a statement in the announcement.

entertainment.title: Kathleen Kennedy Replaces Peter Rice as Head of Ceremonies and Content for L.A.’s Olympic Games (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: "Kathleen is a legend," says LA28 chairperson and president Casey Wasserman in making the appointment while the veteran producer called the Olympics "a touchstone in my life."
entertainment.body:
When news broke that Netflix had tapped Peter Rice to replace Bela Bajaria as chief content officer charged with overseeing scripted and unscripted series, film, live events and more in all territories across the globe, it didn’t take long for insiders to wonder how he could lead such a massive portfolio while continuing on with a role as head of ceremonies for the 2028 Olympic games in Los Angeles.

Question no more: Hollywood veteran Kathleen Kennedy has been tapped to replace Rice as head of ceremonies and content for LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The executive producer role will find the iconic producer helping shape the opening and closing ceremonies for back-to-back games in four separate events that will be viewed by an audience of billions across the globe.

LA28 confirmed the appointment today, and revealed that Rice won’t be bowing out completely as he will stay on as executive producer. Kennedy is expected to dive straight in and work from early development toward production and execution alongside a team that includes executive producer and creative director Ben Winston, and veteran Olympic and Paralympic ceremonies producer Scott Givens who serves as executive producer of production. The production of the Olympic and Paralympic ceremonies is being supported by FulFive, a new entity composed of Fulwell Entertainment and FiveCurrents.

Kennedy is among the most accomplished and successful producers in Hollywood with more than 100 credits on her resumé dating back to the early 1980s. She’s an Oscar winner whose films snagged 120 Academy Award nominations and 25 wins, and she’s steered special effects-heavy blockbusters in the Star Wars universe to character studies and comedies, and dozens of projects alongside her husband Frank Marshall at their Kennedy/Marshall Company. She recently became something of a free agent after departing her post at Lucasfilm earlier in 2026 after 14 years at the helm leading one of the biggest American film franchises.

LA28 chairperson and president Casey Wasserman had plenty of praise for his new head of ceremonies.

“Kathleen is a legend. She is one of Hollywood’s all-time greats, with a rare gift for storytelling,” said Wasserman. “When the stars align to focus the world’s attention on Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, I can’t think of anyone better to conjure the magic of Hollywood than Kathleen.”

In response, she credited Wasserman for having a “bold vision” for what the games “can mean for Los Angeles and the world.” And she’s thrilled to play a part in the Olympics, which have been a big part of her life for decades.

entertainment.title: Art of Elysium Gala to Celebrate Rock Photographer Henry Diltz
entertainment.summary: John Mayer and McG will co-chair the Dec. 12 event, which will also honor Rain Phoenix.
entertainment.body:
Nonprofit The Art of Elysium will celebrate legendary rock photographer Henry Diltz at its upcoming gala on Dec. 12.

The event, held at Hollywood’s Chaplin Studios, has tapped Diltz as its Heaven Visionary. As part of the honor, he will curate a one-night-only art installation representing his idea of heaven — in Diltz’s case, a lush environment reminiscent of Laurel Canyon and Woodstock where he shot many of his most recognizable photos.

Diltz’s has photographed iconic artists and bands including America, The Doors, The Eagles, James Browne, James Taylor, Joni Mitchell, The Mamas & The Papas, The Monkees and Neil Young. His work has appeared on a variety of album covers, cementing his legacy as one of the most celebrated photographers in rock history. Related Stories Lifestyle A Sense of Home Gala to Honor Co-Founders Georgie Smith and Melissa Goddard Movies Sian Heder Used Her "Moment of Power" After Winning an Oscar to Get 'Being Heumann' Made

“Henry has a remarkable gift for making people feel comfortable enough to reveal who they are, and that spirit is at the heart of The Art of Elysium ’s work: bringing artists and communities together to create moments of connection and possibility,” Jennifer Howell, founder and CEO of The Art of Elysium, said in a statement. “We’re honored to have him as this year’s Heaven Visionary and support him as he brings his world to life at Chaplin Studios, where he shares a rich legacy of imagination and storytelling with the musicians who’ve created many of the world’s iconic recordings.”

The event is being co-chaired by John Mayer , Alix and McG Nichol, Faryal Ganjehei and Sima Morrison. Musician Rain Phoenix — sister of Joaquin and River Phoenix — will also receive organization’s Spirit of Elysium honor for her work on behalf of the communities The Art of Elysium serves. Elijah Wood and Chris Holmes will hop into the booth as the night’s DJs.

Funds raised during the evening will support the organization’s focus on helping people who are navigating illness, isolation, displacement, disability, emotional challenges and major life transitions with connection, belonging, dignity, participation and expression.

entertainment.title: John Carpenter to Receive ACE’s Golden Eddie Filmmaker of the Year Award
entertainment.summary: Bonnie Koehler and Christopher Nelson will receive ACE Career Achievement Awards.
entertainment.body:
Filmmaker John Carpenter will receive the American Cinema Editors’ ( ACE ) Golden Eddie Filmmaker of the Year award at this year’s ceremony on Feb. 6, 2027.

The annual ACE Eddie Awards will be held at UCLA’s Royce Hall, where winners in 14 categories honoring editing achievements in film and TV will be announced. Patton Oswalt will return to host the awards show.

Carpenter’s credits include classics such as Halloween (which became the most profitable independent film of its time and launched a franchise), The Fog, The Thing, Escape from New York, Big Trouble in Little China, They Live, Christine, Prince of Darkness, In the Mouth of Madness, Vampires and Escape from L.A , among others. He is considered one of the most influential filmmakers in the horror and genre spaces of all time. Related Stories Movies Academy CEO Bill Kramer Makes the Case for a More Global Oscars at Tokyo Film Festival General News The Hollywood Reporter Tops National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards With 96 Noms, More Than Any Other Outlet

“John Carpenter makes movies that get under your skin and stay there,” ACE President Sabrina Plisco, ACE, says. “ Halloween , The Thing , Escape from New York — these films have scared, thrilled and shaped generations of audiences and filmmakers alike. Few directors understand rhythm, tension and restraint the way he does, and he has always trusted his editors to help him find it. That collaboration is exactly what this honor celebrates.”

Additionally, Bonnie Koehler, ACE, and Christopher Nelson, ACE, will receive career achievement awards.

Koehler has edited 15 feature films and nine television series, and her sound work includes The Empire Strikes Back, Return of the Jedi, Poltergeist , and more. Her feature credits include Heart of Dixie , Curtis Hanson’s Bad Influence , Brian De Palma’s Raising Cain , Shirley MacLaine’s Bruno , and Donald Petrie’s Grumpy Old Men and The Associate . Her TV credits include Law & Order: Special Victims Unit , which earned her a 2004 Eddie nomination, along with Law & Order: Criminal Intent , Deadline , The Grid , House M.D. , Crossing Jordan , In Plain Sight and Eureka .

Nelson has served as a producer, director and film editor on cable and network movies, pilots, series and feature films. He won a Primetime Emmy for editing the series finale of Lost , and has received nominations for Six Feet Under , China Beach , Mad Men and the Greatest American Hero pilot. Having more than 50 TV movies and pilots to his name, his more recent works include Bates Motel , When We Rise , Waco , The Terror , Godfather of Harlem and Queen Sugar .

entertainment.summary: The 15-year-anniversary edition of JLo's seventh studio album is due out next month.
entertainment.body:
Jennifer Lopez is gearing up to celebrate the 15th anniversary of her seventh studio album, Love? , with the LP’s first-ever vinyl release. The rebooted set, which will come in three different collectible editions, will also feature the new dance song “Proof of Love.” Explore Jennifer Lopez See latest videos, charts and news

Lopez told Variety that she was inspired to write and record the new song after her twins, Max and Emme (who recently changed their name to Oskar), left for college this fall. “They take up such a big part of your brain for so long, and when they’re gone, which is devastating and sad and scary, you’re facing a life that’s totally different now, and you’re like, ‘What am I going to do with this space and this time?’ For me, I just went back in the studio,” she said. “I’ve written some of the best songs that I’ve ever written, and I’m really excited. It’s a very happy era album. It’s some of the most joyous, beautiful songs that have just a tad of a tear in them.” Related Foo Fighters Deliver a Blast From the Past on 'Kimmel': Watch ABBA's Mamma Mia! Lopez told Variety that the new track is ” a beautiful song about this kind of duality. It’s this happy dance song, and these are the things that are the proof of love. One of them is pain and grief when someone’s gone. You feel pain and grief. That’s really proof of love. I wanted to make that a happy thing. Fans can pre-order the three vinyl editions now, which will include the standard 12-track version featuring “Proof of Love,” a deluxe 2LP edition with 17 tracks on translucent royal blue vinyl, the new single, new artwork and five additional album tracks: “Hypnotico,” “Everybody’s Girl,” “Charge Me Up,” “Take Care” and “On the Floor (Ven a Bailar).”
