entertainment.title: Travis Kelce Reacts to Prince William Saying He Tried to ‘Move Him Out’ of Royal Family’s 2024 Selfie With Taylor Swift
entertainment.summary: “I get it, man,” the tight end quipped.
entertainment.body:
Travis Kelce understands why Prince William was trying to shake him off from the royal family’s photo op with Taylor Swift .

On the episode of New Heights posted Wednesday (Oct. 28), the Kansas City Chiefs tight end and Jason Kelce reacted to the future King of England telling Graham Norton that he’d tried to move Travis “out of the photo” when the prince snapped a selfie with the pop star and his two eldest children in 2024. “I get it, man,” the younger Kelce brother said with a smile. “I think we all get it.”

“I was just a boyfriend at that point,” he continued. “I wasn’t her husband yet. We don’t really know if this is gonna last, so it’s kinda just, ‘Move out of the way real quick so we can keep this photo forever.’”

“‘Hopefully this doesn’t go south,’” Travis also joked. “‘Otherwise, this photo is not gonna be as good.’”

Though the prince may have had something else in mind, the selfie he did get with son Prince George, daughter Princess Charlotte, Swift and Travis actually ended up being even more historical than it would’ve been without the football player in frame. Taken during the 14-time Grammy winner’s run of Eras Tour shows in London, the group photo ended up being the first snap with Travis that Swift ever posted on her account.

“I hadn’t appreciated the significance, and actually, I was trying to move him out of the photo,” William quipped of the selfie being Swift and Travis’ hard launch on the Friday (Oct. 23) episode of The Graham Norton Show . “But Travis kept coming back in, and I couldn’t work out why he kept coming back in. I was trying to move him out so it was just me and Taylor and the children.”

Luckily, Travis knows it’s not personal. He even offered to send the royals an edited version of the pic after Jason suggested they could Photoshop him out. “I gotta ship that to him,” the Grotesquerie star joked. “Just send it to Buckingham Palace. You think it’ll get to him?”

The episode comes as the 2026-27 NFL season is ramping up, with the Chiefs winning all but one of their games so far. (They lost Oct. 25 to the Seahawks, after which the Seattle team shaded Swift and Kelce on social media.) The musician has been in attendance at every one of Kansas City’s home games so far, most recently appearing in her suite at Arrowhead stadium alongside Este Haim and Caitlin Clark to cheer the team on against the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 18.

entertainment.title: Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson Scare Up a Wickedly Spooky Dance to a Britney Spears Classic on ‘DWTS’: Watch
entertainment.summary: The pair's contemporary dance inspired by the Saw film franchise earned a perfect score on Tuesday (Oct. 27).
entertainment.body:
It was a frightfully entertaining night on Dancing With the Stars on Tuesday (Oct. 27) when the show got into the Halloween spirit a few days early on a “Horror Movie Night”-themed episode. And nobody nailed the combination of scares and flawless steps more than Glee alum Harry Shum Jr. and his professional dance partner Jenna Johnson.

Shum hit the stage in a blood-soaked white shirt and tie, his face dripping with viscera as Johnson stalked him across the floor in a look inspired by the Saw horror franchise. Dancing to 2WEI’s cover of Britney Spears’ 2004 hit “Toxic,” the pair did a high-energy contemporary routine full of daring lifts, spins and one impressive move where Johnson sat on Shum’s shoulder and then lay down flat to form a human “T” shape.

The acrobatic routine rushed to a conclusion with Johnson grabbing Shum and ripping off his tie, sending the actor crashing to the ground, convulsing, as each attempt to get up was met by his partner repeatedly shoving him down with her foot. The dance ended on the creepiest of notes, with Saw ‘s Billy the Puppet rolling onto the stage on his squeaky tricycle.

The dance clearly landed with the judges, with guest adjudicator Shirley Ballas saying she’d “never seen anything like it” and Bruno Toniolo dubbing it “perfect,” leading to the first 40/40 perfect score of the season so far.

Because there was no elimination during last week’s “Dedication Night,” two stars were sent packing on Tuesday, marking the last dance for The Bachelorette ‘s Tyler Cameron and his partner Sharna Burgess — who did a Dracula-themed Viennese waltz to Annie Lennox’s “Love Song For a Vampire” — and Savannah Bananas player Jackson Olson and professional partner Emma Slater, who did a Joker -inspired routine to Frank Sinatra’s “That’s Life.”

entertainment.title: Westwood Recordings Enters JV With Monstercat, With Eye on Artist Development & Global Reach
entertainment.summary: The partnership is being spurred by a $50 million investment in Monstercat by Create Music Group, which acquired the label in 2025.
entertainment.body:
Canadian independent electronic label Westwood Recordings has entered a joint venture with fellow Canadian electronic label Monstercat.

The partnership will provide Westwood with access to capital, global infrastructure (including monthly royalty accounting, global digital distribution and a gaming partnerships department) and an expanded team. Westwood will continue to be based in Vancouver and run by its founder, Nick Middleton .

Middleton, one half of longstanding electronic duo The Funk Hunters, founded Westwood Recordings in 2013 as a home for bass, electronic and hip-hop. The imprint’s roster includes Big Gigantic, Dirtwire, Cut Chemist, Flamingosis, Maddy O’Neal and Chali 2na. Beyond releases, the label has done branded events and stage takeovers at British Columbia music festivals Shambhala Music Festival and Rifflandia and Vancouver’s Malkin Bowl, an outdoor venue in the city’s Stanley Park.

The partnership is part of a broader expansion spurred by Monstercat’s 2025 acquisition by Create Music Group, which invested $50 million in the label — funding that contributed to the new venture with Westwood.

As part of the joint venture, Monstercat will support Westwood in signing new artists and recordings, expanding its release schedule, entering new genres and pursuing catalog acquisitions. The partnership will also support the launch of a publishing arm, building on Westwood’s history in synch licensing.

“I’ve always respected how Monstercat has built its business, especially how transparent they are with their artists and how connected they are to their fans. Those things matter a lot to me, and we’ve built Westwood with that same care,” Middleton said in a statement. “After more than a decade of running Westwood independently, I know how much the right support can mean for an artist or a record. This partnership gives us the backing to put more behind the music we believe in, be more ambitious with the artists and projects we take on, and open more doors for the people we work with. We’ve built something special with Westwood, and there’s a lot more I want to do. After years of working together, the trust I have in Daniel and the Monstercat team is a big part of why this feels right. They understand what we’re building and want to help us take it further.”

“Nick has a real talent for discovering and developing artists, and he’s done an incredible job of that with Westwood,” added Monstercat president Daniel Turcotte . “By combining his A&R instincts and deep roots in the Canadian music industry with Monstercat’s global infrastructure and investment, we have an opportunity to build in new genres and develop artists in spaces we haven’t explored before. I’m excited to build on what Nick has created and see where we can take it together.”

entertainment.title: TikTok Wants to Help Its Users Find Their Next Must Eat
entertainment.summary: The U.S. joint venture of the social video platform rolled out a new food-focused discovery product as it seeks to build out its business.
entertainment.body:
TikTok ‘s U.S. joint venture is leaning hard into the food creator community, launching a new product called Must Eat that is meant to boost food creators, as well as restaurants, all in service of helping its users find that next must visit place to grab a bite.

The company officially rolled out Must Eat at a reception held at Undercote in New York City Tuesday evening, with Adam Presser, the CEO of TikTok’s U.S. business, hosting food creators in the lounge.

“The first time that I came across FoodTok was actually before I joined the company, it was in the pandemic,” Presser told the attendees. “I came across the feta cheese pasta trend … So we were lucky enough to be able to get a block of feta cheese at that time, and we made the recipe, and it was incredible. And it was that first experience of being able to be watching videos, consuming content, and then translating that into real life experiences. And that journey has only continued on TikTok.

“The ‘lunch in my city’ trend has really driven a lot of momentum,” he continued. “I know some of the creators here have made content around that trend. I have tried it out, it’s fantastic. And over the last several years, we’ve just seen more and more people have this experience of discovering something on the platform and driving their in-real-life experience. I saw a stat last year: More than 27 million Americans went to an independent restaurant, cafe, or store in the U.S. that they had discovered for the first time on TikTok.”

So, Must Eat. The product is launching in New York, Los Angeles and the Bay Area, highlighting places in two categories: “Everyday Eats” and “Elevated Dining” featuring restaurants that have connected with TikTok food creators. TikTok also partnered with OpenTable to enable reservations at selected locations.

The product, an expansion of “Must GO” (focused on travel), is an example of how TikTok U.S. is trying to carve its own path forward, now 10 months or so into its new ownership structure.

For Presser, it is also a chance to bring his own imprint onto one of the biggest creator platforms in the country.

“I am an L.A. native, and probably like most people that grew up in L.A., I had dreams of working in entertainment, but any hope of working in front of the camera were quickly dashed — I think it was around the eighth grade play. I was assigned the role of lighting director,” he quipped Tuesday, noting that he went on to work in the music industry and later as an executive at Warner Bros. Discovery before joining TikTok some four and a half years ago.

entertainment.title: Environmental Media Association and Its Awards Show to Become Part of Nonprofit United by Nature
entertainment.summary: The inaugural United by Nature Awards will be held in April 2027 to coincide with Earth Month.
entertainment.body:
It’s a new era for the Environmental Media Association, as the Hollywood sustainability group is becoming a part of nonprofit United by Nature.

EMA has been active in the industry for nearly 40 years, creating conversation through educational initiatives, industry partnerships and events like the Impact Summit and its signature EMA Awards Gala. United by Nature — an organization focused on building the next generation of America’s conservation movement — plans to build upon these programs and relationships, as well as host the first United by Nature Awards in April 2027 to coincide with Earth Month. Related Stories News 'The Wild Robot,' 'The Daily Show' Among Winners at Environmental Media Awards News Stars Talk L.A Wildfires, Home Rebuilds and What to Do With Your Tesla at EMA Impact Summit

“Environmental progress requires a bigger coalition that’s more reflective of communities across America,” Benji Backer, founder and CEO of United by Nature, said in a statement. “EMA proved how powerful storytelling can shape culture, unite people and drive meaningful outcomes for nature. Together, we’re building upon that impact by reaching new audiences and inviting people of all backgrounds to protect the outdoors they love.”

Debbie Levin, the former CEO of EMA who will now serve as chief visionary officer of United by Nature, said, “EMA has always believed in the extraordinary power of entertainment and storytelling to inspire environmental action. For more than three decades, we’ve worked alongside the entertainment community to make sustainability part of the cultural conversation. We’re proud of the legacy we’ve built, and we’re excited to work with United by Nature to reach new audiences and continue making sustainability more accessible and engaging.”

United by Nature’s inaugural takeover of the awards event will continue to celebrate the entertainment industry’s environmental leadership, while also expanding to recognize the individuals and organizations across music, sports, podcasts and universities that inspire positive change. Past EMA honorees include Billie Eilish, Michael Bloomberg, Jane Fonda, Ted Turner, Natalie Portman, Matt Damon and Laura Dern.

The EMA Green Seal will also become the United by Nature Green Seal, which recognizes industries that take meaningful steps to reduce their environmental footprint. Wildwood , the animated fantasy film from Laika Studios, is the first movie to be awarded the United by Nature Green Seal; the movie joins nearly 3,000 other productions recognized for their sustainability efforts.

entertainment.title: Sundance Sets Legacy Screenings Including Films by Christopher Nolan, Justin Lin and Alfonso Cuarón
entertainment.summary: Old will be new again at Sundance 2027. Also fresh: Letterboxd joins as Legacy program co-presenter.
entertainment.body:
As Sundance prepares to write a new legacy in Boulder, Colorado in 2027 and beyond, the film festival is bringing some hits from its past to the new home.

Sundance Institute today revealed the lineup for the Legacy program for next year’s festival, and it includes works by filmmakers including Christopher Nolan, Alfonso Cuarón , Justin Lin , Stacy Peralta, Julie Taymor, Barbara Hammer, Patricia Cardoso and Tom Kalin. While old will be new again, there’s also something fresh for the lineup once known as From the Collection: Letterboxd joins as a co-presenter of the Legacy program with additional details for onsite activations to come. Related Stories Movies Alfonso Cuarón Reflects on Making 'Harry Potter': "Two of the Most Beautiful Years of My Life" 'Awards Chatter' Podcast John Leguizamo on 'The Odyssey,' Non-Traditional Casting and Being Uninvited From 'Spider-Man: Homecoming'

Plucked for the Legacy program — curated as a home to showcase “groundbreaking independent cinema including archival and restoration screenings of fiction and nonfiction works as well as special events” — will feature brand-new restorations of the 2002 Sundance version of Lin’s Better Luck Tomorrow , a digital 4K restoration of Peralta’s Dogtown and Z-Boys , a 35th anniversary screening of Taymor’s Fool’s Fire , Hammer’s Nitrate Kisses , a 25th anniversary screening of Cardoso’s Real Women Have Curves, a star making turn for America Ferrera, a 35th anniversary screening of Kalin’s Swoon , and a 25th anniversary screening of a 4K restoration of Cuarón’s Y tu mamá también, a star making turn for Diego Luna and Gael Garcia Bernal.

Sundance has also set a special two-part session on the final weekend of the festival dubbed “ Sundance Film Festival presents: Cinema Interruptus featuring Memento .” It will feature a 4K restoration and communal discussion for Nolan’s 2000 effort, Memento, starring Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss and Joe Pantoliano.

“We’re excited to kick off the festival season in earnest with this first 2027 Sundance Film Festival announcement, revealing some of our Legacy programming,” explained Eugene Hernandez, who serves as director of the Sundance Film Festival and public programming. “Each year we honor the legacy of our founder Robert Redford and the history of the Sundance Film Festival by looking back at just a few of the films and filmmakers who have shaped our history. Our first festival in our new home in Boulder, Colorado will bring change, but as we evolve, we’ll keep at our core what we celebrate: our rich history.”

entertainment.title: Ezekiel Lewis Talks New Epic Records CEO Gig & the Art of A&R: ‘It’s Not About Genres. It’s About Artists’
entertainment.summary: In the latest episode of Billboard On the Record, Lewis sits down to talk about his new role as Epic's CEO/chairman for the first time.
entertainment.body:
Ezekiel “Zeke” Lewis doesn’t have the typical origin story of a major label CEO. He got his start as a Grammy-winning songwriter and producer in Atlanta, co-penning songs like “One Less Lonely Girl” by Justin Bieber and “The Way I Are” by Timbaland , often with his collective The Clutch, before he made his jump to the boardroom. Today, however, Lewis sees the creative journey as critical to his understanding of the music business and what artists need from their industry partners.

“When I got inside the building, I realized that my songwriting career and the fact that I had achieved some success was a miracle,” he explains. He was fascinated by “the way music moves through buildings,” and he found a new calling to “get inside to help creators” navigate the industry with greater success.

First, he built up his own publishing house, Bar Music Group. Then he landed an A&R gig at Motown Records, where he worked his way up the ladder to become senior vp of A&R by the time he left in 2018. That job was also where he first worked with legendary label executive Sylvia Rhone , who he says taught him to “be diligent, never give up and never take no for an answer,” as he puts it. But when Rhone left the job and took a role at Sony Music’s Epic Records, where she eventually rose to become its CEO/chairman, she courted Lewis to follow her and scout the next generation of talent there.

As Lewis has advanced in his career at Epic, he’s played a pivotal role in shaping the careers of 21 Savage, Madison Beer, BIA, Black Eyed Peas, DDG, Future, GIVĒON, Zara Larsson, Mariah the Scientist, Travis Scott, Southside, Meghan Trainor and Tyla. When Rhone stepped away in 2025, rumors swirled that Lewis was being eyed as her successor. In March, the confirmation finally came that Lewis had been appointed CEO/chairman of Epic.

Lewis joins the latest episode of Billboard On the Record in his first-ever interview as CEO and chairman to discuss what it takes to run a successful label in 2026, how he approaches A&R, and how his songwriting career shaped his leadership in the boardroom.

You have built up your whole business career in music in A&R. This historically has been a role held often by creative people. I think of George Martin, producer and A&R for The Beatles, as a prime example. Now, however, A&R is more data-driven and typically not held by creatives. Why have we moved away from A&R having creative experience?

entertainment.title: Leading U.K. Indies Distiller Records & Speedy Wunderground Launch Label Partnership With New Heartworms Material
entertainment.summary: Distiller Records recently landed its first U.K. No. 1 album with Blossoms' sixth studio effort.
entertainment.body:
Leading U.K. indie record labels Distiller Records and Speedy Wunderground have launched a new partnership.

The new collaboration begins with the release of Heartworms’ new single “Guess I’m Stuck in the Dark,” out Tuesday (Oct. 27).

Under the new partnership, Speedy Wunderground will retain “full creative autonomy over its A&R and production” and utilize Distiller’s “marketing, distribution, and operational scale to amplify its roster further,” per a joint statement.

Speedy Wunderground was founded in London by producer Dan Carey and has been instrumental in shaping the sound of the capital’s indie and alternative scene for the past decade with Black Country, New Road, Squid, Black Midi and Mercury Prize winners English Teacher all releasing early material via the label. In his work as a producer, Carey has credits on studio albums by Fontaines D.C. , Wet Leg and Kneecap , among others.

Distiller, led by managing director James Moodie , recently scored its first U.K. No. 1 album with Blossoms’ sixth studio album Songs From the Wedding Cake . Its roster also includes Reverend & The Makers, Yonaka, Sports Team and The Ramona Flowers. Related Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Jessica Lynch

Heartworms is the moniker for London-based musician Josephine Orme, who released her 2025 debut album Glutton for Punishment through Speedy Wunderground. The album charted at No. 9 on the U.K.’s Independent Albums Chart. She’ll be the lead support act for Interpol and Bloc Party ’s co-headline tour in the U.K. and Europe, beginning Nov. 20 in Birmingham.

Speaking on the collaboration Moodie said, “I’ve always loved what Dan and the team at Speedy Wunderground have built, it’s a respected label brand that is the very definition of creative integrity and credibility. This partnership is about giving each artist a bigger platform, deeper resources, and the backing to push their incredible talents even further.”

Carey added, “It’s a great partnership as the team at Distiller are really experienced and clearly understand the ethos of Speedy and the way we like to work. We’re looking forward to working together on a range of different projects, from very quick turnaround punk records to big campaigns — kicking off with this week’s release from Heartworms.”

entertainment.title: Yahritza y Su Esencia Joins Double P Management Roster: ‘Their Ceiling Is Extraordinarily High’
entertainment.summary: The música mexicana trio will be co-managed by George Prajin and Adriana Martinez.
entertainment.body:
Double P Management, the artist management company led by renowned music executive George Prajin and global superstar Peso Pluma , has added Yahritza y Su Esencia to its management roster, Billboard can announce exclusively on Wednesday (Oct. 28).

Under the new co-management partnership, the chart-topping sibling trio will continue to be represented by longtime manager Adriana Martinez while also working alongside Prajin and his team to support the next phase of their career growth and global expansion.

“Yahritza y Su Esencia have built something truly special. Their talent, authenticity and connection with audiences have already established them as one of the most important young groups in música mexicana ,” Prajin said in a statement. “What makes this partnership so exciting is that they are still at the beginning of an incredibly bright future. They possess a rare combination of artistry, vision and star power, and we believe their ceiling is extraordinarily high. We are excited to work alongside Adriana and help support the next phase of what we expect will be a long and impactful career.”

Martinez added: “Yahritza y Su Esencia have always had something special and tremendous potential. Their talent, work ethic and connection with fans continue to open new doors, and this partnership felt like the right next step. George Prajin shares our vision for the group’s future, and alongside his incredible experience, we’re excited to work together to create a complete ecosystem for Yahritza y Su Esencia and help them continue growing and achieving great things together.”

Since emerging as one of the most influential young acts in regional Mexican music, Yahritza y Su Esencia has captivated audiences with its distinctive sound, emotional songwriting and remarkable commercial success, with songs including “Soy El Único,” “Esta Noche” and “Frágil” with Grupo Frontera. Formed in Yakima, Wash., by siblings Yahritza, Armando and Jairo Martínez, the group has amassed billions of streams, earned multiple chart achievements and established itself as one of the genre’s most recognizable and impactful acts.

In 2022, the band’s five-track EP Obsessed reached No. 1 on Billboard ‘s Regional Mexican Albums chart. That came a month after it scored its first chart entry on any Billboard chart with “Soy El Único,” the set’s lead single, which opened at the summit of the Hot Latin Songs tally.
